- **My team have really been bonding over the World Cup on our WhatsApp chat. Reflecting on England's recent match against Mexico, I found myself thinking about how much we can learn about leadership from sport. The odds were stacked against them. They were playing in front of a hostile crowd, under immense pressure, and then faced an even bigger challenge when they were reduced to 10 players. At that point, it would have been easy to accept defeat. Instead, they dug deep, adapted to the situation and focused on what they could control. It made me think... What's the equivalent of that hostile crowd in your workplace? Is it increased competition? Reduced resources? Organisational change? Or something else entirely? The most successful teams aren't the ones with perfect conditions. They're the ones that stay focused, adapt and keep moving forward when conditions are at their toughest. #Leadership #Teamwork #Resilience ...more**

- **I almost contacted IT this morning. I'd spent 15 minutes trying to find my OneDrive that I use all the time. I searched everywhere and was convinced something had gone wrong. Before raising a support ticket, I decided to ask AI. Within seconds, it showed me that nothing had disappeared. The folder had simply been moved. It made me think about organisational change. When people struggle with change, it is often not because they don't want to adapt. It's because they don't know where things have gone, why they've changed, or what they're supposed to do next. What seems obvious to the people leading the change isn't always obvious to everyone else. Whether you're introducing AI, rolling out new technology, or changing the way a business operates, success depends on more than the technology itself. It depends on bringing people with you through clear communication, guidance and support. A small moment turned into a good reminder that change is much easier when people understand the journey. Has a simple everyday experience ever changed the way you think about leadership or transformation? #Cheemia #Pharma #Leadership #DigitalTransformation #AI ...more**

- **.::Life Update::. - **How many actionable insights do you uncover in a month? And is that normal? We talk about actionable insights as if they are floating around the hospitals, waiting to be harvested. While in reality, gathering a real actionable insight is a lot of work and often a bit of a journey that involves asking the right questions, diving into the data, speaking with several stakeholders and doing a lot of thinking. An actionable insight often starts with a well placed question and some really good listening. But it often requires more than just that one conversation. So don’t be discouraged if you are not bringing in those pearls of wisdom every day. A simple piece of information or a half formed insight can be very valuable as well, as long as you are aware of what it is, and you report it internally in a strong way. Would love to hear your thoughts! PS how cute is this village? I was delivering a training in the south of France and was lucky enough to have some time to wander around.
